entries.subject: Yato

spans.text: Yato kho ahaṁ, aggivessana, kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito, taṁ vata me uppannā vā sukhā vedanā cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, uppannā vā dukkhā vedanā cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassatīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjatī”ti.

entries.description: shaved off my hair and beard
entries.subject: shaved off

spans.text: Ever since I shaved off my hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness, it has not been possible for any pleasant or painful feeling to occupy my mind.”
Why don’t I shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness?’

Some time later, while still with pristine black hair, blessed with youth, in the prime of life—though my mother and father wished otherwise, weeping with tearful faces—I shaved off my hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness.

entries.description: So kho ahaṁ
entries.subject: So

spans.text: So kho ahaṁ, aggivessana, aparena samayena daharova samāno, susukāḷakeso bhadrena yobbanena samannāgato paṭhamena vayasā, akāmakānaṁ mātāpitūnaṁ assumukhānaṁ rudantānaṁ, kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajiṁ.
So kho ahaṁ, aggivessana, nacirasseva khippameva taṁ dhammaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsiṁ.
So kho ahaṁ, aggivessana, nacirasseva khippameva taṁ dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇiṁ.
So kho ahaṁ, aggivessana, tāvatakeneva oṭṭhapahatamattena lapitalāpanamattena ñāṇavādañca vadāmi theravādañca, ‘jānāmi passāmī’ti ca paṭijānāmi, ahañceva aññe ca.
So kho ahaṁ, aggivessana, taṁ dhammaṁ analaṅkaritvā tasmā dhammā nibbijja apakkamiṁ.

entries.description: Then it occurred to me
entries.subject: Then

spans.text: Tassa mayhaṁ, aggivessana, etadahosi: Then it occurred to me, ‘na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi saddhā, mayhampatthi saddhā; ‘It’s not just Āḷāra Kālāma who has faith, na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi vīriyaṁ, mayhampatthi vīriyaṁ; energy, na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi sati, mayhampatthi sati; mindfulness, na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi samādhi, mayhampatthi samādhi; immersion, So evaṁ pabbajito samāno kiṅkusalagavesī anuttaraṁ santivarapadaṁ pariyesamāno yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkamiṁ; upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṁ kālāmaṁ etadavocaṁ: Once I had gone forth I set out to discover what is skillful, seeking the supreme state of sublime peace.

Tassa mayhaṁ, aggivessana, etadahosi: Then it occurred to me, Atha khvāhaṁ, aggivessana, yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkamiṁ; upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṁ kālāmaṁ etadavocaṁ: So I approached Āḷāra Kālāma and said to him, Iti yādiso ahaṁ tādiso tuvaṁ, yādiso tuvaṁ tādiso ahaṁ.

Tassa mayhaṁ, aggivessana, etadahosi: Then it occurred to me, ‘nāyaṁ dhammo nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati, yāvadeva ākiñcaññāyatanūpapattiyā’ti.

At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

Tassa mayhaṁ, aggivessana, etadahosi: Then it occurred to me, ‘na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi saddhā, mayhampatthi saddhā; ‘It’s not just Āḷāra Kālāma who has faith, na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi vīriyaṁ, mayhampatthi vīriyaṁ; energy, na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi sati, mayhampatthi sati; mindfulness, na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi samādhi, mayhampatthi samādhi; immersion, So evaṁ pabbajito samāno kiṅkusalagavesī anuttaraṁ santivarapadaṁ pariyesamāno yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkamiṁ; upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṁ kālāmaṁ etadavocaṁ: Once I had gone forth I set out to discover what is skillful, seeking the supreme state of sublime peace.

Tassa mayhaṁ, aggivessana, etadahosi: Then it occurred to me, Atha khvāhaṁ, aggivessana, yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkamiṁ; upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṁ kālāmaṁ etadavocaṁ: So I approached Āḷāra Kālāma and said to him, Iti yādiso ahaṁ tādiso tuvaṁ, yādiso tuvaṁ tādiso ahaṁ.

Tassa mayhaṁ, aggivessana, etadahosi: Then it occurred to me, ‘nāyaṁ dhammo nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati, yāvadeva ākiñcaññāyatanūpapattiyā’ti.
Realizing that this teaching was inadequate, I left disappointed.

Some time later, while still with pristine black hair, blessed with youth, in the prime of life—though my mother and father wished otherwise, weeping with tearful faces—I shaved off my hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness.
Ever since I shaved off my hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness, it has not been possible for any pleasant or painful feeling to occupy my mind.”
‘Lābhā no, āvuso, suladdhaṁ no, āvuso, ‘We are fortunate
We should both lead this community together.’

Yato kho ahaṁ, aggivessana, kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito, taṁ vata me uppannā vā sukhā vedanā cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, uppannā vā dukkhā vedanā cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassatīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjatī”ti.
“Addhā kho te ayaṁ, aggivessana, āsajja upanīya vācā bhāsitā, “Your words are clearly invasive and intrusive, Aggivessana.
